1ff37e4c567cfe5f66c6db366400f737.interpretation: Earthquake event log (18 rows). Identity='date'. **NB**: 'date' is non-unique (29 april 1955 ×2, 30 august 1955 ×3) — for cell_lookup this is fine when the queried entity is unique (e.g., '27 november 1954' identifies one row); for argmax/argmin via date, ties resolve to the first-occurrence row. Numeric: local magnitude (strict). Other: origin time, epicentre coords, location. **GATING (Migration #1 post-Codex fix)**: argmax/argmin-via-date tools and lifts REMOVED from the menu because `date` is non-unique — tie-resolution would make those ops unsound under R10. Cell_lookup via date is retained: the L1 premise `CellAt r "date" (Value.str name)` is sound when `name` identifies a unique row, and the runtime now enforces that entity matching happens in the identity column (_execute_lookup identity_col kwarg).

Resolution requires runtime eval_cond + parse_mode integration.

5d0f2b303e9271a48109c4d6b80206d8.interpretation: Time series of vital statistics (21 years). Identity = "Unnamed: 0" (year column, each row a year). Average pop / Deaths / Natural change / Crude birth rate / Crude death rate / Natural change (per 1000): all strict. Live births is excluded from numeric tools because cell "1 104" uses thin-space thousands separator that no current parse_mode handles correctly (leading_int would yield 1 not 1104). Treated as count-only via other_columns until runtime gains thousands-space parsing.

US Chart position is leading_int (cells like "17 (R&B)" carry chart annotation). Catalogue No. (strict). Label is text. R1 caveat: count_where lifts on leading_int columns silently exclude annotated cells (eval_cond cannot parse them); a hypothetical query like `count_where col > X` would under-count. Resolution requires runtime parse_mode-aware condition evaluation.

4b4ff8f17963fa7ba3edd5cae2c32abb.interpretation: NFL season records (32 rows). Last row "totals :" is an aggregate footer, NOT a team. Setting identity_column=None for argmax/argmin disables entity-anchored argmax/argmin so a hypothetical "team with most wins" claim does not return "totals :" as a verified team. cell_lookup is enabled separately via identity_column="team" — it emits HasProperty (cell-level fact), so looking up "totals :" returns the footer's aggregate values correctly (this is true at the cell level, distinct from the entity-level argmax misinterpretation we avoid). Aggregate ops (sum/mean/count) over numeric cols include the footer in their totals — for the current gold (sum wins where win_pct > 0.7), the footer's 0.623 win_pct excludes it from the filter. Numeric all strict.

4cc489011d65d97a1a1c269bbcdd112d.interpretation: Video poker payouts (13 hand types + 1 footer). Last row "theoretical return" is a percentage-valued summary, NOT a payout hand. Setting identity_column=None for argmax/argmin disables entity-anchored argmax/argmin (which would otherwise return "theoretical return" as the hand with max payout). cell_lookup is enabled separately via identity_column="hand" — it emits HasProperty (cell-level fact), so looking up "theoretical return" returns the footer's percentage values correctly (true at cell level, distinct from entity-level misinterpretation). Aggregate sums over credit columns will include the footer percentages mixed with payout values — solvers should be aware. Numeric all strict (auto-strips %).

65aadc9add4b1a42f5b5071d6a16cfd6.interpretation: Triple-block table (3 blocks of Year/Number/Name; pandas auto-suffixed duplicate column names → Number/Number.1/Number.2). Goal queries first 'Number' column (canonicalizes to 'number'). No single-entry cell_lookup: the row-as-3-records structure means lookup-by-name cannot be sound — cell_lookup applies to ANY column, so a lift over Name=identity could certify cross-block facts like (block-1 Name) → (block-2 Number.1), which is false. Either no lift or block-scoped lookup is needed; for Tier 1 we accept the asymmetry (this is the one table without cell_lookup; 119/120 coverage). identity_column=None disables entity-anchored argmax/argmin too. Numeric: Number, Number.1, Number.2 (all strict). Year/Year.1/Year.2 are time ranges (strings). Name fields text.
